notes.title: New biomes
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

First off, we want to thank you for the amazing reception our game is getting! As a small team with no marketing experience, it's been tough getting this project in front of people—but your wonderful comments keep us going.

Progress is coming along smoothly, and we've just updated our trailer to showcase more areas you'll be able to explore in Battle Plan: Jester’s Knife. After completing the tutorial area, you'll have the freedom to explore these locations in any order you choose. Along the way, you'll meet unique characters and pilot a variety of vehicles, each with its own abilities.

notes.title: Devlog #7
notes.content:
Hi everyone,
Progress on the game is chugging along.

We are currently implementing a badge system in the game. You will be able to unlock these badges and equip them in game. They can modify your character's stats or change/add specific abilities during combat so that you can use your preferred character in your preferred playing style.

The fighting tutorial is finished and we should be soon testing it to check user-friendliness.

Our second character's fighting animation is now finished. Loredana is a young witch who floats on a stick attached to a skull's head. She is obsessed with [REDACTED] and her main objective in life is to [REDACTED] back to [REDACTED]. Can you believe that?!

notes.title: Devlog #6
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

It has been a while since our last update, and we wanted to share some exciting progress with you.

Firstly, our combat mechanics are nearing completion, and we have put in a tremendous amount of effort into perfecting our character animations. We are proud to announce that all animations will be crafted using traditional frame by frame 2D animation. This applies not only to our fighters but also to the Jester, who will play a crucial role in the game. The Jester will be responsible for presenting each round, performing the countdown, indicating the time remaining for the round, and even signaling whose turn it is in turn-based mode.

We have been considering participating in the current Steam Next Fest, but after careful consideration, we have decided against it. The reason behind this is that we are simultaneously working on a captivating map overworld that will allow you to explore between each fight. Within this overworld, you can expect to encounter puzzles, enemies, and even formidable bosses. As a result, we believe that the game requires a bit more time in the development process. However, rest assured that we plan to release a demo once this aspect of the game reaches a presentable state.

Lastly, we would like to express our gratitude to all the people who have already wishlisted our game. This is our first venture into game development, and your support and encouragement mean the world to us. Your unwavering enthusiasm has truly bolstered our spirits as we navigate the challenges that come with creating a game.

Thank you once again, and we look forward to providing you with more updates soon.

See you in our next update!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947117/4fe9ef02342416b4bef52db4ae572ae11f158a56.gif[/img]

notes.title: Devlog #5
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We're excited to announce the latest update to our game. We've been working hard to improve the gameplay experience, and we're happy to say that we've made some significant progress.

First off, we've introduced stop frames to animations. While fighting, characters will now stop on an attack tile that deals damage. This helps to make the hits feel more powerful and exciting.

In addition, we've improved the health bar animation to make it easier for players to keep track of their progress. The new animation is more intuitive, and it provides a clear visual indication of how much health each player has left.

We've also introduced a small frame around the tiles to show the player its condition. Red means the tile will lose, orange means it will tie, and green means the tile will win. This makes it easier for players to know the result of their strategy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947117/00ce664b91b639fb65ed570c6b427b7d7de06c64.png[/img]

We've updated the win and lose character animations to make them more exciting and impactful. Currently, they are more of a placeholder but we do believe that winning or losing a match should feel like a big deal, and these animations will help to convey that feeling.

Finally, we've introduced character combos. Each character will now have a specific combo that can be used to perform more powerful attacks. These combos are based on specific tile arrangements, and they add a new layer of depth and strategy to the game.

We're really happy with how the game is coming along, and we hope you are too. Thanks for your support, and we can't wait to see you in the game!

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947117/def2085ceb0af259e597b7f1eb3dbcc331a854dd.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947117/f1eb4b059229f979c791edd471241c4cfcec4ca0.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Devlog #4
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

It's been a while since our last update, but we wanted to let you know that a lot of work has been done behind the scenes.

First off, we decided to explore multiplayer. We believe that adding a multiplayer mode to the game will be a great addition, and it will allow players to compete against each other and have even more fun. Working remotely, we are taking advantage of the opportunity to test it easily.

We've also started integrating Steamworks API to be able to use their peer-to-peer connection. This will make it easier for Steam players to play against their friends or compete in a public lobby. We also explored 'Unity Relay' to handle the peer-to-peer connections, which can be easily changed without disrupting the flow of the game.

In addition, we've implemented win-and-lose conditions for the game.

While not many visible changes can be seen in this update, rest assured that we're working hard to deliver the best possible experience to our players. We're excited about the progress we've made and can't wait to share the game with you all.

Thanks for your continued support

notes.title: Devlog #3
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We've been hard at work on our game project, and I wanted to share some exciting updates with you all.

After testing the last build, we decided that we should explore different game modes to add more variety to the gameplay. So, we've been working on implementing two new game modes: turn-based and one-tile turn.

In the turn-based mode, players take turns sliding tiles on the board. This is a great option for players who want to take their time and plan out their moves carefully. In the one-tile turn mode, players can only move one tile per turn, which adds a new level of strategy to the game.

The best part is that these game modes can be mixed and matched as desired before starting the fight, including their time limits individually. This will allow players to customize their experience and create the perfect game mode for them.

To make it easier to test these different game modes, we've implemented more debug controls. This will save us time during development and ensure that we're delivering the best possible experience to our players.

We're excited about the progress we've made so far and can't wait to share the game with you all. Stay tuned for more updates as we continue to work on it!

notes.title: Devlog #2
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We've been making great progress on our game project, and I wanted to share some updates with you all.

First, we've been working on the puzzle input controls so that they can be easily changed from player to bot or vice versa. This will give players the flexibility to choose how they want to play the game.

Additionally, we've introduced the first "dumb" bot, which randomly slides tiles on the board. This is the first step towards creating more intelligent bots that will provide a greater challenge for players.

After testing the previous build, we discussed and decided to include a new mechanic where, with every hit, a random tile starts to break. If the tile takes three hits, it gets stuck, and you cannot move it for the next round. It adds a new layer of strategy to the game, and players will have to think carefully about which tiles they want to attack.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947117/9e252e21579fbdf2442f9f186d1c2ae933fc85ab.png[/img]

It's important to note that you cannot have more than one stuck tile and another with one damage after a round since the maximum number of hits a player can take is four. This is to ensure that players have a fair chance to recover from attacks and strategize for the next round.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947117/44ed9f53f4c124bd087a527171098f8cb75fe52a.png[/img]

Finally, we've implemented character animations in this build and tested them extensively. We're excited about how the game is coming together and can't wait to share it with you all.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947117/14859822486641ccdcdd7037e4953b0ebf001bba.png[/img]

notes.title: Devlog #1
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

I'm excited to share the progress we've made on our latest game project! We've created the first simple prototype of the game and have been playtesting it to refine the gameplay mechanics.

Currently, the gameplay involves both players sliding tiles on their boards to counter the other player's moves. The game is designed to be fast-paced, and both players play simultaneously with a time limit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947117/63d42e44c059ba7bc2c8ab83a4b12045afa57168.png[/img]

There are four types of tiles that players can use: Block, Punch, Jump, and Kick. Additionally, there are four types of counters: Punch wins against Jump, Jump wins against Kick, Kick wins against Block, and Block wins against Punch.

The attack tiles are Punch and Kick, and at the end of the timer, the characters will be animated fighting. If an attack-type tile wins, the opponent will take damage to their health. The player with zero health will be defeated. This feature is not yet implemented, but we are working on it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947117/735691a9340fbc2cc25ccee348b96a7b078c5d35.png[/img]

We're excited about the progress we've made so far and can't wait to share the game with you all once it's ready. Stay tuned for more updates as we continue to work on it!
